dataset_name: AZH Wound and Vascular Center dataset
source: AZH Wound and Vascular Center, Milwaukee, WI (via uwm-bigdata GitHub)
num_patients: Not stated exactly (\"most images from separate patients\"; some patients have multiple images at different sites/healing stages)
classes: venous, diabetic, pressure, surgical (NO arterial class)
class_distribution: Not published per-class in README (would need to unzip Train.zip/Test.zip and count)
patient_ids_available: No (no patient_id CSV shipped; some same-patient repeats acknowledged but not enumerated)
metadata_available: Yes - body-map location annotations shipped as BodyMap.zip
license: Not explicitly stated on repo (no LICENSE file found in repo root); dataset released alongside two peer-reviewed Sci Rep papers
public_accessibility: Public - directly downloadable, no request needed
download_method: git clone / direct download of dataset/Train.zip and dataset/Test.zip from github.com/uwm-bigdata/wound-classification-using-images-and-locations
known_limitations: No arterial class at all; no patient-ID file so leakage across train/test zips (as shipped) cannot be independently verified; class counts not documented in README, must be derived from the zips directly; single clinic (Milwaukee) - limited demographic/geographic diversity
existing_papers_using_dataset: Anisuzzaman 2022 Sci Rep; Patel 2024 Sci Rep; multiple follow-on wound-classification papers cite it as 'the AZH dataset'

source: Same as AZH, merged with Medetec stock images by UWM Big Data Lab
original_publication: Same UWM Big Data Lab papers as above
classes: diabetic, pressure, surgical, arterial+venous (COMBINED into one class - not separated)
class_distribution: Not published; arterial and venous are merged so cannot be used for a 3-way venous/arterial/diabetic split
metadata_available: Partial (inherits AZH body-map for AZH-sourced images only)
license: Same ambiguity as AZH + Medetec's own unclear terms
public_accessibility: Public in principle (same repo family) but not confirmed as a separate downloadable archive in the repo we inspected
download_method: Not directly verified - would need explicit confirmation from repo maintainers or paper supplementary material
known_limitations: Arterial and venous ulcers are merged into a single class, which defeats the specific research goal of separating them; provenance/quality of Medetec-sourced images is weaker than AZH's clinical labeling
existing_papers_using_dataset: Referenced in the same UWM Big Data Lab paper family as 'AZHMT'

source: University Hospital Regensburg, Germany (Dept. of Plastic/Hand/Reconstructive Surgery + Dermatology)
original_publication: Neuwieser et al. 2025, Diagnostics 15(17):2184 (doi.org/10.3390/diagnostics15172184), CC BY 4.0 article text
num_patients: 72 (patients with purely arterial or purely venous ulcers; mixed arterial-venous ulcers explicitly EXCLUDED)
image_resolution: avg height 833px, avg width 742px, jpg, manually cropped to wound ROI + 10% margin
patient_ids_available: Yes at the study level (72 patients identified
metadata_available: IRB-approved retrospective pull by ICD code) but no public patient_id-to-image mapping file has been released
license: Yes within the paper (inclusion/exclusion criteria, per-patient healing-stage repeats documented) but not shipped as a machine-readable file
public_accessibility: Paper text is CC BY 4.0, but the IMAGE DATA ITSELF IS NOT: Data Availability Statement says 'For data supporting reported results, please contact the corresponding author' (sally.kempa@ukr.de)
download_method: NOT public - access requires directly emailing the corresponding author and is not guaranteed
known_limitations: Email request to corresponding author; no automated/scripted download exists
existing_papers_using_dataset: Image access is gated behind a manual author request with no guarantee of approval or turnaround time; no diabetic class; single-center (Regensburg) retrospective cohort; small arterial class (198) limits statistical power; mixed arterial-venous ulcers were excluded from the source cohort entirely so real-world 'mixed etiology' cases are not represented
column16: This is itself the primary paper introducing/using this dataset (Neuwieser et al. 2025); it cites Huang et al. 2023 (J Plast Reconstr Aesthetic Surg 79:89-97) as a related 5-class study on a different, also-unverified-availability dataset

dataset_name: Lower Limb and Feet Wound Image Dataset (currently in research/data/raw/)
original_publication: Md Masudul Islam et al., Mendeley Data DOI 10.17632/hsj38fwnvr, v3
num_patients: Not available (no patient ID file shipped)
classes: normal, wound (binary only - the source paper describes 8 wound sub-types [diabetic, pressure, trauma, venous, surgical, arterial, cellulitis, other] but the public archive does NOT ship per-image sub-type labels)
metadata_available: No per-image sub-type or patient metadata ships with the archive
public_accessibility: Public - directly downloadable, sha256-verified in this repo's scripts/fetch_dataset.py
download_method: python scripts/fetch_dataset.py (already implemented in this repo, verifies sha256 against Mendeley's published hash)
known_limitations: No sub-type labels in the actual download despite the source paper describing 8 categories - CANNOT be used for venous/arterial/diabetic classification without re-labeling; no patient IDs so train/val/test splits are stratified image-level only (leakage across splits cannot be ruled out, documented in this repo's own README)
existing_papers_using_dataset: Already the dataset in active use in this repo (research/); documented in research/README.md

original_publication: DFUC2021 challenge dataset, associated with multiple MICCAI/DFUC workshop papers
classes: diabetic foot ulcer pathology classes only (e.g. infection / ischaemia presence-absence) - NO venous or arterial classes
metadata_available: Public on Zenodo (per search results; not independently fetched in this pass)
license: Not verified in this pass (would need direct Zenodo page fetch)
public_accessibility: Diabetic-only scope - cannot support venous/arterial distinction; would only ever supplement the diabetic class in a combined dataset, and combining across studies/institutions risks a strong non-biological 'source' confound the classifier could latch onto instead of true ulcer pathology

dataset_name: Medetec Wound Database (leg ulcer image sets)
original_publication: No formal peer-reviewed dataset paper - a curated stock-image gallery
num_images: ~85 images visible on the leg-ulcer-images gallery page alone (exact venous vs arterial split not machine-readable from the page); total across all wound categories on the site not tallied in this pass
class_distribution: Venous and arterial leg ulcers (two separate gallery pages / 'sets'), diabetic foot ulcers, pressure ulcers, and 12 other unrelated wound categories (burns, abdominal dehiscence, etc.)
image_resolution: Not machine-readable; images are presented as an HTML photo gallery, not as labeled folders or a metadata table
public_accessibility: Site states images are 'free stock images' / 'freely reproduced' subject to conditions on a separate page - exact license terms not machine-verified in this pass and should be re-checked before any use
download_method: Public - freely browsable and (per site's own description) downloadable
known_limitations: Manual browsing and per-image download from HTML gallery pages; no bulk-download or archive file exists
existing_papers_using_dataset: No structured labels or class folders - would require substantial manual curation and per-image labeling before use; image quality is inconsistent (site notes some images were digitized from 35mm transparencies with mould damage); no patient/provenance metadata; small counts per class; not a peer-reviewed research dataset
column16: Occasionally used as a supplementary/study-adjacent source in other papers (e.g. combined into AZHMT above) but not a standalone benchmark in the literature we found
